_readme: One fixture set per prompt version, keyed by prompt id, pinned to a sha256.
The sha256 is the whole mechanism. When the prompt file changes, its hash no
longer matches what is written here, the prompt is reported `stale`, and the
score it had is NOT carried forward. Re-blessing is deliberate: read the diff,
decide the cases still describe what the prompt must do, then write the new
hash in. `uv run desk prompts` prints the current hashes.
A case supplies the fields the prompt takes and asserts what must survive
rendering. These are offline structural checks and spend no tokens. They catch
the two things that actually go wrong: a placeholder was renamed, so every
caller now raises; or an edit quietly deleted a load-bearing instruction, such
as the sentence telling the model that posting text is untrusted.
The fields in each case are exactly the fields the call site passes — see
desk.analyst.extract, desk.analyst.families, desk.analyst.reflect,
desk.analyst.score and desk.tailor.tailor. That is deliberate and it is what
makes the second check work in both directions: a placeholder the prompt gains
and the call site does not pass raises KeyError here, and a placeholder the
prompt loses drops a sentinel value out of the rendered text and fails a
must_contain. Keep the field lists in step with the call sites, not with what
would be convenient to write.
Prompts with no entry here are reported as unmeasured, never as passing. The
ten versions of the pipeline's own prompts are covered — normalizer,
orchestrator, resolver, analyst and tailor. baseline/single_agent_turn.v1 is
deliberately absent: it was being written while these sets were pinned, and
pinning a hash to a file somebody is still editing reports staleness rather
than quality. It gets a fixture set once its author settles it.
